rationale: At depth 4, below the limit 6, two reusable one-sided elimination obligations merit separate proofs. After moving the pivot to (0,0), the parent applies column clearing; preservation of the first row then supplies the divisibility hypothesis for row clearing. It takes C to be the resulting trailing block and composes the units with the permutation matrices. The children have independent proofs, require neither a nonzero pivot nor a determinant hypothesis, and neither restates the full parent theorem.

subproblems.title: Clear a divisible first column while preserving the first row
subproblems.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, m a natural number, and B a matrix indexed by Fin (m + 1) in both directions over R. Suppose B(0,0) divides B(i.succ,0) for every i : Fin m. There exists a matrix U of the same size, invertible under matrix multiplication, such that (UB)(0,j) = B(0,j) for every j : Fin (m + 1) and (UB)(i.succ,0) = 0 for every i : Fin m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (m : ℕ) (B : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R), (∀ i : Fin m, B 0 0 ∣ B i.succ 0) → ∃ U : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R, IsUnit U ∧ (∀ j : Fin (m + 1), (U * B) 0 j = B 0 j) ∧ (∀ i : Fin m, (U * B) i.succ 0 = 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Put p = B(0,0). For each i : Fin m, divisibility supplies a coefficient a(i) with B(i.succ,0) = p a(i). Since R is commutative, B(i.succ,0) = a(i)p as well. Choose these coefficients simultaneously.
2. Define a square matrix N using Matrix.of: its zeroth row is zero, and N(i.succ,j) equals a(i) if j = 0 and zero otherwise. Thus every column of N except column zero is zero, and N(0,j) = 0 for every j.
3. For arbitrary row s and column t, expand (N N)(s,t) as the sum over k of N(s,k)N(k,t). When k = 0 the second factor is zero; when k ≠ 0 the first factor is zero. Every summand vanishes, so N N = 0.
4. Set U = I - N and W = I + N, with I the matrix identity. Distributing matrix multiplication gives U W = I + N - N - N N = I and W U = I - N + N - N N = I. Consequently U, with inverse W, defines a unit of the matrix ring, so IsUnit U holds for matrix multiplication.
5. The multiplication formula gives (N B)(0,j) = 0 and (N B)(i.succ,j) = a(i)B(0,j), because only the summand with intermediate index zero can remain. Therefore (U B)(0,j) = B(0,j) and (U B)(i.succ,j) = B(i.succ,j) - a(i)B(0,j). Taking j = 0 yields (U B)(i.succ,0) = a(i)p - a(i)p = 0.
6. These identities and the unit from step 4 give every required conclusion. If m = 0, the coefficient family is empty, N is zero and U is the identity, so the same construction and all the assertions remain valid.
proof_key_steps: Choose coefficients expressing the lower entries of column zero as multiples of B(0,0).
Put these coefficients in column zero of a matrix N whose zeroth row vanishes.
Show N squared is zero by inspecting each multiplication summand.
Exhibit I + N as a two-sided inverse to U = I - N.
Compute UB to prove preservation of the first row and vanishing below the pivot.

subproblems.title: Clear a divisible first row without changing the trailing block
subproblems.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, m a natural number, and H a matrix indexed by Fin (m + 1) in both directions over R. Suppose H(i.succ,0) = 0 for every i : Fin m and H(0,0) divides H(0,j.succ) for every j : Fin m. There exists a matrix V of the same size, invertible under matrix multiplication, such that HV has entry H(0,0) at (0,0), zero at (0,j.succ) and (i.succ,0), and entry H(i.succ,j.succ) at (i.succ,j.succ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (m : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R), (∀ i : Fin m, H i.succ 0 = 0) → (∀ j : Fin m, H 0 0 ∣ H 0 j.succ) → ∃ V : Matrix (Fin (m + 1)) (Fin (m + 1)) R, IsUnit V ∧ H * V = Matrix.of (fun i j => Fin.cases (Fin.cases (H 0 0) (fun _ => 0) j) (fun i' => Fin.cases 0 (fun j' => H i'.succ j'.succ) j) i)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Put p = H(0,0). For each j : Fin m, choose b(j) with H(0,j.succ) = p b(j), using the assumed divisibility.
2. Define a square matrix M using Matrix.of by M(0,0) = 0, M(0,j.succ) = b(j), and M(i.succ,t) = 0 for every i : Fin m and t : Fin (m + 1). Column zero is zero, and every row other than row zero is zero.
3. In the sum expressing (M M)(s,t), the term with intermediate index k = 0 vanishes because M(s,0) = 0. Every term with k ≠ 0 vanishes because row k of M is zero. Thus M M = 0. Set V = I - M and W = I + M. Distributivity yields V W = I + M - M - M M = I and W V = I - M + M - M M = I. This gives a unit of the matrix ring with value V and inverse W, hence IsUnit V for matrix multiplication.
4. Since column zero of M is zero, (H M)(s,0) = 0. In column j.succ, only intermediate index zero contributes, so (H M)(s,j.succ) = H(s,0)b(j). Therefore (H V)(s,0) = H(s,0) and (H V)(s,j.succ) = H(s,j.succ) - H(s,0)b(j).
5. Step 4 gives (H V)(0,0) = p and, by the first hypothesis, (H V)(i.succ,0) = 0. For the top row it gives (H V)(0,j.succ) = p b(j) - p b(j) = 0. For the remaining block the first hypothesis gives (H V)(i.succ,j.succ) = H(i.succ,j.succ) - 0 b(j) = H(i.succ,j.succ).
6. Every index in Fin (m + 1) is either zero or a successor. The four cases in step 5 therefore prove, entry by entry, equality with the nested Fin.cases matrix in the conclusion. Together with the unit from step 3 this proves the assertion. For m = 0 the coefficient family is empty, M is zero, and the same identities apply without any nonvanishing assumption.
proof_key_steps: Choose coefficients for the off-pivot entries of row zero.
Place these coefficients in row zero of a matrix M with column zero vanishing.
Prove M squared is zero and obtain V = I - M as a matrix unit.
Compute right multiplication by V using the unique possible summand at intermediate index zero.
Use the zero first-column hypothesis to preserve the trailing block and identify all four Fin.cases entries.
